scope: Compare current local DWG/DXF parser hardening checks with open-source coverage-guided fuzzing practice; identify actionable harness and crash-triage refinements without increasing per-slice validation or changing format-support claims.

method.kind: Primary-source web review plus read-only local plan, source, CMake and workflow inspection
localInspection: tests/hardening_tests.cpp:testDxfReadFuzzSmoke and testDwgReadFuzzSmoke generate deterministic pseudo-random byte vectors with fixed iteration and length bounds
.github/workflows/build.yml:long-fuzz selects only the extended deterministic test on scheduled/manual Linux GCC runs
Repository search found no LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput or AFL target in the current checkout
DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md:PAR-12/S13 already owns deterministic hardening and scheduled fuzz-related policy
method.evidenceRule: Peer harness defects and fuzzing configurations are design signals, not local defects or capabilities. Deterministic generated-input tests are not coverage-guided mutation fuzzing. Parser safety findings require direct-route reproduction; fuzz execution, corpus growth, non-crashing parses, and self-roundtrips do not establish semantic support.

evidence.topic: LibreDWG uses distinct parser and conversion-oriented fuzz routes
evidence.observed: Current project guidance describes AFL++, honggfuzz and LLVM/libFuzzer paths. The documented modes distinguish DWG, ASCII DXF, binary DXF and conversion routes; dwgrewrite exercises decode-encode-decode. The guidance also describes sanitizer use and replay of saved failures.
doesNotEstablish: behavior of a pinned peer executable on a local input
semantic correctness of rewrite or self-roundtrip output
that external peer corpora are eligible local fixtures
evidence.planUse: Use route separation, sanitizer/replay organization and explicit outcomes as optional design patterns only. Do not make peer installation or a long fuzz campaign a per-slice prerequisite.

evidence.topic: Fuzz harness defects can dominate reported crashes
evidence.observed: The closed issue describes a double-free in LibreDWG's -rw/-indxf fuzz harness and reports that the harness defect generated about 1,573 crashes before being isolated. The report identifies the issue as harness-only.
doesNotEstablish: a parser crash in every reported input
that current LibreDWG has the same defect
evidence.planUse: Add harness self-validation and direct-reader replay before classifying a fuzz signal as a library finding; keep harness errors separate from parser outcomes.

evidence.topic: Coverage-guided mutation needs structured-input seeds and bounded scheduled execution
evidence.observed: LLVM documents the LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput byte-span target, coverage-guided corpus retention, and the value of varied valid/invalid seeds for structured input. A list of existing corpus files can be replayed without fuzzing. This is distinct from deterministic pseudo-random loops.
doesNotEstablish: license or fixture eligibility for any third-party input
that a coverage-guided target is required for this repository
semantic support from new coverage or a non-crashing execution
evidence.planUse: Consider a separate optional Clang target only when a named parser-coverage gap justifies it; seed from locally authored builders, isolate generated corpus under temporary storage, and keep the route out of ordinary builds.

evidence.topic: Local long-fuzz naming should not imply coverage-guided mutation
evidence.observed: The local smoke functions synthesize deterministic pseudo-random input in memory. The opt-in CTest is built and invoked by a fixed scheduled/manual Linux GCC workflow. No LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput or AFL target was found in the checkout.
doesNotEstablish: absence of parser bugs outside generated input coverage
any feature, format, consumer or geometry support claim
evidence.planUse: Describe the existing test as deterministic generated-input fuzz/safety smoke; retain fast focused validation per implementation slice and the current scheduled cadence.
